body.estimand_functional: \(\theta_G=F_G(\operatorname{vech}\Sigma)\), with minimum recursive certificate degree \(ID_G\) and graph-uniform frontier \(D_2(n)\)

sampling_model.design: Independent observational sampling from a fixed acyclic linear Gaussian structural equation model.
sampling_model.units: \(X_1,\ldots,X_N\) are independent copies of the observed \(n\)-vector.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment; the causal target is the full supported structural mechanism.
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; regularity is stated through covariance, rational-denominator, and influence-covariance margins.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate \(\Sigma\) by \(\widehat\Sigma\), differentiate the deterministic rational output \(F_G\), and estimate the joint influence covariance by empirical plug-in averaging. At a sample denominator pole use the zero evaluation convention; at a pole or singular \(\widehat V_F\), return \(\mathbb R^r\) as the confidence set.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For prespecified \(d\geq ID_G\), the degree-bounded algorithm returns minimum-degree formulas; Propositions 7.2 and 7.3 bound half-trek and instrumental-cutset certificates by \(2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}+1\), and Proposition 7.4 bounds auxiliary-cutset certificates by \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^4+2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^3+s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^2\), yielding \(5\), \(5\), and \(36\) at \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}=2\).
The half-trek criterion is a polynomial-time sufficient criterion for rational identification by recursive linear systems.
Instrumental cutsets give a sound graphical identification criterion for linear structural causal models.
Auxiliary cutsets enlarge the efficiently certifiable subclass by recursively using identified coefficients as auxiliary information.
A missing cycle in a directed-tree model yields a quadratic equation, and multiple cycles can select one rational root.
Every directed-tree structural coefficient is generically one-identifiable, two-identifiable, or unidentifiable, and the classification is complete.
The complete tree-only identification predicate can be implemented in randomized \(O(n^3\log^2n)\) time.
A Cohen--Macaulay graph or Rees algebra yields inverse-degree bounds through regularity and Jacobian-dual minors.
Generic identification in unrestricted linear structural causal models has a sound and complete polynomial-space decision procedure.
Fixed half-trek estimators have recursive influence functions, asymptotic normality, and plug-in Wald inference.
Bow-free path recovery is stable under quantitative conditions, while a four-node example has unbounded condition number.
At a vanishing constraint gradient, the Wald statistic can converge to a nonstandard rational function of a Gaussian vector.

body.tldr: For every rationally identifiable acyclic linear Gaussian mixed graph on \(n\) observed vertices, cubic graph-ideal generators and Dubé's Gröbner-degree theorem give the explicit unconditional bound \(ID_G\leq U_2(n)=2\cdot8^{2^{n(n+1)}}\). Lexicographic extraction is proved here and produces a direct certificate for every structural and disturbance coordinate, so \(B_2(n)=U_2(n)\) yields a total exact call to the degree-bounded identification algorithm. The sharp full-class question is now the honest bounded-versus-unbounded elbow for \(D_2(n)\): the proposed windmills are excluded because they are generically infinite-to-one. For the six-vertex two-triangle graph, choosing the shared coefficient as the seed proves \(ID_{K_6}\leq7\), while exactness remains open pending a hash-addressed closure transcript. Fixed-chart inference is logically separate and applies to any fixed deterministic rational map on its regular chart.

project_justification.gap: Hollering, Misra, and Sturma's formula-producing algorithm requires a supplied degree cutoff. Their subclass bounds are \(2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}+1\) for half-trek and instrumental cutsets and \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^4+2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^3+s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^2\) for auxiliary cutsets, hence \(5\), \(5\), and \(36\) at \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}=2\). The effective cutoff proved here makes the full-class search total, but no result decides whether the sharp frontier \(D_2(n)\) is bounded uniformly in \(n\), nor its least constant or growth rate.
project_justification.niche: Directed indegree two is the first sparse class in which missing-covariance equations can couple multiple incoming coefficients. The exact recursive closure quantifies over every identifying order, including disturbance-coordinate shortcuts, while the full-class elbow separates an effective double-exponential termination bound from the still-unknown intrinsic formula degree.
project_justification.fill: The note proves a cubic presentation of the covariance graph ideal, applies the published Dubé bound, and derives the lexicographic step that extracts direct \(q a(s)-b(s)\) certificates of degree at most \(U_2(n)\). This compiles into an unconditional total formula-returning schedule. It also proves \(ID_{K_6}\leq7\) by cancelling two central-seed quadratics. The exact \(K_6\) degree and the sharp bounded-versus-unbounded frontier remain explicit certified-computation and structural-algebra questions; the disproved windmills are not used as a lower family.

body.related_work: Hollering, Misra, and Sturma define \(ID_G\), return minimum-degree rational formulas below a prespecified cutoff, and give the half-trek and instrumental-cutset bounds \(2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}+1\) and the auxiliary-cutset bound \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^4+2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^3+s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^2\). Dubé's general Gröbner-basis theorem supplies the published double-exponential degree bound used for the new unconditional full-class cutoff; the lexicographic extraction to direct SEM certificates is proved in this note. Foygel, Draisma, and Drton provide the half-trek baseline, and Kumor, Chen, and Bareinboim and Kumor, Cinelli, and Bareinboim provide the two cutset criteria. Van der Zander et al., Gupta and Bläser, and Briefs and Bläser develop the tree and missing-cycle mechanisms adjacent to the \(K_6\) calculation, but they do not determine its source-defined recursive degree. Dörfler et al. give a total generic-identification decision benchmark without the same rational formula output. Mareis, Sturma, and Drton are retained only as adjacent fixed-estimator inference work: the regular-chart delta-method and simultaneous Wald theorem here is for an arbitrary fixed deterministic rational map and has no logical dependency on the stopping schedule.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The bound \(U_2(n)=2\cdot8^{2^{n(n+1)}}\) is an effective elimination bound, not a sharp estimate of \(D_2(n)\). The proof \(ID_{K_6}\leq7\) supplies no lower bound, no auxiliary-cutset failure result, and no substitute for the required exact filtered-closure artifact. The former two-parent windmills are generically infinite-to-one and cannot support any lower bound on the rationally identifiable class. No replacement dimension-feasible birational family or theorem deciding whether \(\sup_nD_2(n)\) is finite has been established.
body.honest_scope: The established structural results are the recursive closure characterization, the exact values \(D_2(1)=1\), \(D_2(2)=2\), and \(D_2(3)=3\), the unconditional inequality \(D_2(n)\leq U_2(n)\), the corresponding total exact stopping schedule, and the upper bound \(ID_{K_6}\leq7\). The exact value of \(ID_{K_6}\), any claim that \(K_6\) lies outside auxiliary cutsets, the bounded-versus-unbounded elbow, and a matching lower family remain open. The old padded windmills are expressly excluded from the identifiable class. The inference theorem remains fixed-dimensional and regular-chart, assigns the full ambient set on pole or singular covariance events, and applies to a fixed deterministic rational map independently of how that map was selected or computed. No semiparametric efficiency, adaptive-selection validity, growing-dimensional Gaussian approximation, singular-chart coverage, or sharpness of \(U_2\) is claimed.
